extracted.intended_audience: New York City residents, voters, and people interested in charter revision commissions
extracted.subtask_description: Informational summary of the New York City Charter and the role, scope, and outputs of Charter Revision Commissions; points users to key documents from recent commissions. Useful for people wanting to understand how charter amendments are reviewed and proposed to voters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and purpose of the New York City Charter
rubrics_metrics.description: The New York City Charter defines the organization, functions, and essential procedures and policies of our City government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the Charter as the foundational document governing city organization, functions, procedures, and policies; establishes what a revision commission is reviewing when it examines the Charter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Charter Revision Commissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Charter revision commissions are temporary commissions that review the entire Charter and put any proposals for its amendment before the voters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the commissions' temporary status and their duty to both review the Charter comprehensively and submit proposed amendments to a public vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of proposed amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A charter revision commission may propose a broad set of amendments that essentially 'overhauls' the entire Charter, or may narrowly focus its proposals on certain areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that commissions have flexibility in scope — from full-scale overhauls to narrowly targeted changes — which affects the form and breadth of proposals presented to voters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of key documents
rubrics_metrics.description: This website provides key documents from several recent charter revision commissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points readers to primary source materials (reports, meeting records, proposals) from past commissions as resources for understanding prior processes and proposals.
